decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach to the two inner upright supports; use slow coordinated tilt and watch actual geometry.
Align both open grippers above inner supports. Height and centers are estimated from calibrated head RGB; finish approach before closing.
Use wrist views to refine forward alignment, descend to support grasp height, then close. Retention remains unverified until lift.
Lift both closed grippers to verify retention, then bring supports toward a symmetric base location. Preserve upright attitude.
Lower retained supports back onto the table, release, and withdraw gently to inspect the base spacing.
Withdraw from released supports and turn the open grippers toward opposite ends of the long board, staying on each arm's own side.
Complete board-grasp orientation using smaller rotations after the continuity rejection; keep the open grippers above the board ends.
Approach both ends of the long board with matched descent and close only at the grasp pose. Confirm retention on the next lift.
Hold both grippers closed, then lift the board evenly above support height to verify a stable two-ended grasp.
Carry the level board forward above both upright base supports, then begin a small matched descent.
Set the lower board gently across the two supports, open both grippers, then separate upward and outward to check stability.
The lower board appears stable on both supports. Move clear and reorient toward the two remaining white supports for the middle layer.
Finish the support-grasp orientation while approaching above each remaining block, with open fingers and conservative descent.
Refine block alignment from wrist RGB: shift left outward and forward, right outward and back, while descending slowly with fingers open.
Advance to center the supports between the fingers at grasp height, then close both grippers. Verify retention before transporting.
Lift the closed grippers clear of the table to verify both supports are retained, then begin moving inward above lower-board height.
Both white supports remain visible between the fingers after lifting. Transport them inward, level and above the completed lower layer.
Center the middle supports at symmetric positions over the lower board, then begin a slow descent while retaining both pieces.
Lower the middle supports onto the lower board, release gently, and retreat a little before checking that both remain upright.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for motion. Withdraw from the released supports and begin turning toward the shorter board.
Both middle supports appear upright. Finish turning the grippers square to the shorter board ends while descending to a safe pre-grasp height.
Descend evenly to the shorter board's end-grasp height, then close both grippers without moving the board sideways.
Maintain both closed grasps and lift the shorter board evenly clear of the table; verify retention before moving over the tower.
The shorter board is retained at both ends. Add clearance and carry it level over the two middle supports, centered above the lower board.
Lower the centered middle board onto its two upright supports, pause for seating, then open both grippers without disturbing the layer.
Withdraw from the released middle board. Move each arm outward toward its remaining top piece, keeping both elbows up and increasing downward gripper tilt slightly.
Approach the green top piece from the left and the small wooden board from the right, open grippers, stopping above estimated grasp height for visual refinement.
Refine top-piece grasp positions using the wrist views and close cautiously. The small board's wide span may require a different approach if it is not retained.
Lift both top pieces with closed grippers to check retention. Keep the left piece clear while preparing to orient and place the small wooden board first.
Green piece is retained, but the small board stayed on the table. Hold green clear and rotate the right gripper to grasp across the board's narrower dimension.
Hold the green piece steady. Finish rotating the right gripper across the narrow board width and descend to a visual pre-grasp.
Align the right fingers with the small board's narrow width using wrist RGB, descend cautiously, and close. Keep green stationary and retained.
Lift the newly grasped small board, then begin turning it to span left-right while carrying it inward. Green remains held clear of the tower.
The small board is visibly retained. Continue its level inward transport and yaw alignment above the middle layer, keeping the green piece aside.
Finish centering and squaring the small board above the middle layer, then lower cautiously toward its seating height.
Make a small centering correction, seat and release the top wooden board, then lift the right gripper clear while the green piece stays retained.
The small wooden board appears seated and centered. Clear the right arm and carry the green top piece inward above the tower without crossing the arms.
Correct the rejected tensor from the unchanged observation: center the green piece, descend slightly, and return the cleared right arm toward origin.
Seat and release the centered green top piece, withdraw gently, and finish bringing the right arm to its origin. Verify tower stability after release.
The green piece remains on the top board after release. Withdraw the left arm safely away from the tower and begin returning it to origin with both grippers open.
All eight pieces appear upright and centered. Finish the left arm's continuous return to origin, keeping both grippers open and clear of the tower.
